parts:
Hi Listers,

I am a complete beginner with ggplot and only marginally more experienced with R in general.

I have been struggling to produce a nice scatterplot with a 2nd order polynomial regression fitted including 95% confidence intervals. I did get what I wanted under the generic plot function in R but wanted something a bit more publication quality.

Here is what I tried

> qplot(SOI,u_average,data=soi.currents.edited,geom=c('point','smooth'),method='lm',formula=u_average~poly(SOI,2,raw=TRUE))

Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'u_average' not found

> soi.currents.edited
      SOI    u_average
1   -28.5 -0.241330663
2   -25.4 -0.251319320
3   -24.4 -0.215724327
4   -24.2 -0.290679083
5   -24.1 -0.155357754
6   -23.5 -0.254288315
7   -22.8 -0.133241939...........

I cannot see why the error message has occurred. The scatterplot comes up OK but no polynomial regression and errors?

Any help appreciated.

Andy

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: plotting polynomials
parts:
What I usually do is calculate the upper and lower bounds of CI and pass those values to geom_smooth. Something along the lines of 

...
geom_smooth(model.pred, aes(ymin = lcl, ymax = ucl, fill = habituation, colour = habituation),
            stat = "identity", alpha = 0.1) +
...

where ymin and ymax represent the aforementioned bounds. Fill and colour are there for making things pretty and stat should be set to "identity" to tell ggplot2 to not bother calculating anything but to take your values. Alpha is set to something rather transparent. model.pred is the data.frame with (at least) columns lcl and ucl.

Cheers,
Roman

>
> thanks
>
> Andy

By setting fill=NA you have turned off the plotting of the confidence
intervals ... try

geom_smooth(method='lm',formula=y~poly(x,2),colour='red')

(se=TRUE is the default anyway, and there's not need to go out of your
way to use a raw polynomial -- the predictions will be the same)

Ben Bolker
